subject: chemistry

concepts.title: Mass Percentage
concepts.definition: The mass percentage represents the grams of a specific component contained within one hundred grams of the total solution.
concepts.key_idea: Relative mass fraction expressed as a percentage.
question_patterns: calculate the mass percentage of the solute
find the mass percent of component in solution
what is the mass percentage if mass is given
determine the concentration in mass percent
compute the mass percentage of the mixture

solution_steps.explain: divide component mass by total mass and multiply by 100

concepts.title: Molarity
concepts.definition: Molarity measures the concentration of a solution by the number of moles of solute present in one liter of the total solution volume.
concepts.key_idea: Moles of solute per unit volume of solution.
question_patterns: calculate the molarity of the solution
find the molar concentration of the solute
what is the molarity of solution containing given mass
determine molarity given volume and moles
compute the molarity of the aqueous mixture

solution_steps.explain: divide mass of solute by its molar mass
divide moles by volume in litres

concepts.title: Molality
concepts.definition: Molality defines concentration as the number of moles of solute dissolved in exactly one kilogram of the solvent.
concepts.key_idea: Moles of solute per kilogram of solvent.
question_patterns: calculate the molality of the solution
find the molal concentration of the solute
what is the molality of given mass in solvent
determine molality using solute moles and solvent mass
compute the molality of the mixture

solution_steps.explain: divide mass of solute by its molar mass
divide moles by solvent mass in kilograms

concepts.title: Henry's Law
concepts.definition: Henry's law states that the partial pressure of a gas above a liquid is directly proportional to its mole fraction within that liquid.
concepts.key_idea: Gas solubility is proportional to pressure.
question_patterns: calculate the partial pressure using Henry constant
find the mole fraction of gas in solution
what is the Henry law constant for the gas
determine the solubility of gas at given pressure
compute the gas concentration using Henry law

solution_steps.explain: divide partial pressure by Henry constant

concepts.title: Raoult's Law
concepts.definition: Raoult's law states that for a solution of volatile liquids, the partial vapour pressure of each component is proportional to its mole fraction in the liquid phase.
concepts.key_idea: Vapour pressure of component depends on its mole fraction.
question_patterns: calculate the partial vapour pressure of component
find the total vapour pressure of the mixture
what is the vapour pressure of the solution
determine the mole fraction from vapour pressures
compute the total pressure using Raoult law

solution_steps.explain: multiply pure vapour pressure by mole fraction for each component

concepts.title: Elevation of Boiling Point
concepts.definition: The boiling point of a solution increases when a non-volatile solute is added, proportional to the molality of the solution.
concepts.key_idea: Boiling point rises with solute concentration.
question_patterns: calculate the elevation in boiling point
find the new boiling point of the solution
what is the boiling point elevation constant
determine the molality from boiling point change
compute the boiling point of the mixture

solution_steps.explain: add elevation to pure solvent boiling point

concepts.title: Depression of Freezing Point
concepts.definition: The freezing point of a solvent decreases upon the addition of a non-volatile solute, proportional to the solution's molality.
concepts.key_idea: Freezing point drops with solute concentration.
question_patterns: calculate the depression in freezing point
find the new freezing point of the solution
what is the freezing point depression constant
determine the molality from freezing point change
compute the freezing point of the mixture

solution_steps.explain: subtract depression from pure solvent freezing point

concepts.title: Osmotic Pressure
concepts.definition: Osmotic pressure is the excess pressure required to prevent the flow of solvent into a solution through a semipermeable membrane.
question_patterns: calculate the osmotic pressure of the solution
find the molarity from osmotic pressure
what is the osmotic pressure at given temperature
determine the molar mass using osmotic pressure
compute the pressure required to stop osmosis

solution_steps.explain: multiply molarity by gas constant and temperature

worked_examples.question_pattern: Calculate the molarity of a solution containing {mass} g of NaOH in {volume} mL solution.

solution_template.explain: mass divided by molar mass of NaOH (40)
moles divided by volume in litres

worked_examples.question_pattern: Calculate the freezing point depression for {mass} g of ethylene glycol in {solvent_mass} g of water.

solution_template.explain: mass divided by molar mass of ethylene glycol (62)
moles divided by solvent mass in kg
